components.name: Individual oral

ia.name: Individual oral
ia.limit: 15 minutes: 10 min prepared response + 5 min teacher questions (30% SL, 20% HL)

criteria.name: Knowledge, understanding and interpretation
look: Shows secure knowledge of both extracts and the whole works or body of work they come from
Makes interpretations that are clearly tied to the chosen global issue
Supports every claim with precise, well-chosen references to the extracts and wider works

criteria.name: Analysis and evaluation
look: Explains how specific authorial choices (language, structure, form, visual features) present the global issue
Evaluates how effective those choices are, rather than just naming techniques
Treats the literary and non-literary texts with balanced depth

criteria.name: Focus and organization
look: Keeps the global issue at the centre of the whole 10 minutes
Follows a clear, balanced structure with signposted movement between the two texts
Ideas build on each other and connect the extracts to their wider works

criteria.name: Language
look: Speaks clearly and accurately with a confident, appropriate register
Uses precise literary and analytical vocabulary naturally
Varies sentence structure and avoids reading from a script

checklist: My global issue is specific, has real-world significance and is visible in both texts
One text is a literary work and the other a non-literary body of work, both studied in class
Each extract is no longer than about 40 lines (or a comparable portion of a visual text)
I bring clean copies of both extracts and an outline of no more than 10 bullet points
My introduction names the global issue and both texts and explains why they are paired
I spend roughly equal time on each text and link each extract to its whole work or body of work
Every point analyses an authorial choice and its effect, with a quoted or located reference
I have timed a rehearsal at close to 10 minutes without reading from a script
I have prepared for follow-up questions that push me to extend or justify my points
I have not used either text for my HL essay or for Paper 2 works

examTips: In Paper 1, answer the guiding question but go beyond it: build a clear thesis about purpose and effect, then analyse how specific features create that effect.
Name the text type and its conventions early (e.g. op-ed, infographic, charity appeal) and show how the writer uses or breaks them for a particular audience.
In Paper 2, compare throughout. Organise by ideas, not by work, and make every paragraph link both works to the question with precise textual references.
Technique spotting earns little: for every device, quote it, explain its effect on the reader and tie it back to the writer's purpose or the question.
Plan before you write. Five to ten minutes spent on a thesis and paragraph order usually improves focus and organization, which is worth up to a quarter of the marks.
